guides.title: Declare CMS resources as data
guides.summary: defineResource() declares fields, indexes, access rules, ownership and explicit migration steps; the planner turns declarations into additive FastDB DDL.
guides.markdown:
A resource is plain data, so it can live in application code or a plugin manifest. Field builders map to one FastDB field type and CHECK each: `string`, `text`, `enum`, `integer`, `bigint`, `number`, `boolean`, `datetime` (Unix milliseconds), `reference`, `json`, `list`, `vector` and `blocks`; `field.slug(from)`, `field.terms(taxonomy)` and `field.media()` build a unique slug derived from another field, indexed term IDs and a media file ID. Options include `required`, `nullable`, `default`, `max`, `min`, `pattern`, `unique`, `index` and `search` (full-text). Records are stored in a strict collection `r__<owner>__<name>` with host fields for revision, operation, timestamps and owner. `schemaless: true` types only the host fields in the database and validates the rest in the host, so field changes need no DDL; collections use it.

Access rules per action are `public`, `authenticated`, `owner` (needs `ownership: true`), `{ permission }`, `{ where: { field: value } }` (records whose fields match, such as published posts), `{ any: [...] }` or `none`. Unlisted actions require `<resource>:<action>`, for example `app/tickets:update`. Field `access` hides or locks single fields.

`cms.plan()` reads the live catalog through INFO and plans additive DDL: new collections, optional fields and indexes. A changed type, a new required field or a tighter rule is blocked until an explicit step covers it: `backfill`, `tighten`, `rename` (keep the old field declared) and, in a later release, `drop`. `cms.migrate()` applies each step as one atomic batch with `ifSequence` from the planning read, records it in the `cms_migrations` ledger with the exact SQL and engine release, and re-plans when another write lands first. A failed step rolls back and its resource stays inactive.

guides.title: Read and write records through repositories
guides.summary: Repositories authorize every call, compile bounded parameterized FastQL, and write the record, revision, audit row and outbox event in one atomic batch.
guides.markdown:
`createCMS({ db, modules, resources, plugins, storage })` builds the host; `cms.resource(id)` returns a repository with `get`, `list`, `count`, `countMany`, `search` (full-text over `search: true` fields), `create`, `update`, `delete` and `revisions`. `where` takes a value, `{ ne }`, `{ in }`, ranges (`gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`) and, on indexed lists such as terms, `{ contains }` or `{ containsAny }`; `order` and `offset` give numbered pages, `after` cursor pages. Empty slug fields are derived from their source field, and taken slugs get `-2`, `-3`, …. Every call takes the request principal. Owner rules become query conditions, and owner-scoped search computes allowed IDs first and checks every hit again in the same query. Public shapes are JSON-safe: `{ id, rev, createdAt, updatedAt, owner, ...fields }`, with bigint fields as decimal strings.

A mutation is one atomic batch. An edit carries `expectedRevision`; a stale revision, lost access or a concurrent edit of the same record fails with `CMS_CONFLICT` and writes nothing else, because the revision, audit and outbox rows are guarded by the operation ID the record statement wrote. Before the batch, `cms.resource.before-write` filters can adjust or reject the draft under a deadline. After commit, `cms.outbox.dispatch()` delivers `cms.resource.after-commit` events and retries only the plugins that failed. An unconfirmed write fails with `CMS_UNCERTAIN` and is completed by `db.recoverPending()`.

guides.title: Define collections, blocks, taxonomies, settings and media
guides.summary: Collections are content types defined as data and stored schemaless; blocks fields hold typed content blocks; taxonomies group entries by nested terms; settings and media are host services.
guides.markdown:
A collection, such as `products`, is the resource `cms/<name>` built from a `CollectionDefinition`: label, title, generated slug, publishing (draft, pending review, scheduled, published, trash), nesting through `parent`, taxonomies, a public URL `path` and fields. A `path` of `''` serves entries at the site root, as WordPress's "Post name" permalinks do: root entries share one slug namespace with other root collections, archive bases and the application's `reservedPaths`, and `cms.archiveUrl(collection)` finds where a root collection's archive lives (for posts, the Reading settings' posts page). Posts and pages are built-in collections in `contentModule`; administrators add collections and fields with `cms.saveCollection(definition, principal)`, which needs `cms:collections`. Each collection is its own document table without `STRICT`: saving changes only indexes and records the declaration hash with the stored definition in one step. Built-in collections keep their core fields and accept added ones; their `fieldOrder` places the module's fields among the added ones, and new fields go last. Every collection also has `seo` (a `field.group()` of title, description, social image, canonical URL and noindex), `locale` and `translationGroup`; one with `comments: true` has `commentsOpen`. When a package upgrade changes a built-in collection or adds host tables, `ready()` applies them on the next request. Hosts call `await cms.ready()` per request to load definitions; a write that finds a newer definition reloads it first.

A `blocks` field holds an ordered list of `{ id, type, data }`. `CORE_BLOCKS` are paragraph, heading, image, gallery, quote, list, code, button, embed and divider; plugins add types in their manifest's `blocks`. A block type names a Solar `icon` and a `category` from `BLOCK_CATEGORIES` (text, media, design, widgets, embeds; default widgets), which the editor's block picker groups by. The host validates every block's data against its type on write. A required text field must not be blank.

`cms.taxonomies` keeps terms with a materialized path of ancestor IDs: `create`, `update` (a move rewrites the subtree in one statement), `delete` (children move up), `tree`, `subtree`, `ancestors`, `counts` and `ensure` (tags typed by name). Records hold term IDs in indexed arrays, so `{ containsAny: await cms.taxonomies.subtree(id) }` lists a category and the categories below it. `cms.saveTaxonomy()` adds vocabularies.

`cms.settings` stores validated groups (General, Media, Writing, Reading and those modules add), cached per isolate. `cms.files` (with `storage`) accepts uploads whose declared type matches the file signature, records image size, alt text and captions, and lists the library by kind.

guides.title: Build themes, menus and rich text content
guides.summary: Themes are plugins with site templates and options; menus are revisioned trees resolved for visitors; rich text fields store validated ProseMirror JSON rendered to escaped HTML.
guides.markdown:
Themes are plugins, as extensions are in VS Code. A plugin manifest's `theme` field declares the label, menu `locations` (such as `primary` and `footer`) and `options`, settings fields shown under Appearance → Customize and stored as `<plugin>.<option>`. The plugin's `ui.ts` exports `theme`, a `SiteTheme`: `layout`, `entry` and `archive` templates, optional `home`, `search`, `notFound` and block overrides. Templates get plain views (`SiteView`, `EntryView`, `ArchiveView`, resolved `MenuItemView` trees) and `ThemeHelpers` (`options`, `content(parts)`, `block(block)`, `isActive(url)`); they never read the database. `cms.themes()` lists them with their `problems`, `cms.activeTheme()` resolves the `appearance.theme` setting to a usable theme, and `cms.activateTheme(name, principal)` switches it at runtime. Theme templates need no grant; a theme's resources, hooks and network access follow the plugin grant. `cossack add cms` renders `src/plugins/default-theme/` as application source. A manifest's `logo` and `cover` name images in the plugin's `assets/` (default `assets/logo.*` and `assets/cover.*`); the Plugins and Themes screens show them, or initials and a gradient when a plugin ships none. A plugin that only ships a theme has nothing to grant and counts as active.

`cms.menus` stores each menu's items as one JSON tree with a revision: `create`, `update(id, { name, items }, { principal, expectedRevision })` (a stale revision is `CMS_CONFLICT` and writes nothing), `delete`, `place(id, locations)`, `assign(location, id | null)` and `forLocation(location)`, which resolves entries and terms by ID to their current titles and URLs for visitors, hides unpublished or deleted targets and is cached per isolate. Items are `link`, `entry`, `archive` or `term`; `menuProblems` validates them (300 items, 5 levels). The editor works on rows: `flattenMenu`, `buildMenu`, `moveRows`, `dropDepths` and `shiftRows` implement drag-and-drop and the move buttons. All of this needs `cms:appearance`.

A `field.richText()` field stores a ProseMirror (TipTap) document, `{ type: 'doc', content }`. `checkRichText` and the repository accept only the declared nodes, marks and attributes, with safe link and image URLs; top-level `cmsBlock` nodes embed blocks validated like a blocks field. `richTextHtml` renders escaped HTML, `richTextParts` splits a document at its blocks for themes, `richTextPlain` and `richTextExcerpt` give its text. A searchable rich text field indexes its plain text, kept in `_text_<field>`. Posts and pages use rich text bodies.

guides.title: Write a CMS plugin within its manifest
guides.summary: A plugin's manifest declares resources, hooks, permissions, network hosts, slots and commands; its server.ts registers handlers through a context limited to those declarations.
guides.markdown:
`cossack add plugin` renders a plugin package into `src/plugins/<name>/`. The manifest (`plugin.json`) declares `resources`, `blocks` (block types named `<plugin>/<name>`), `hooks` (extension points and versions), `permissions.resources` (access to resources the plugin does not own), `permissions.network` (hosts), `permissions.define` (new permissions), `ui.slots` links and `commands`. `server.ts` exports `register(context)`: `context.hooks` accepts only declared extension points, `context.commands.add` only declared commands, `context.cms` reaches only the plugin's resources and granted ones, and `context.fetch` only granted hosts. Plugin pages under `src/plugins/<name>/pages` route like application pages; pages under `pages/dashboard/` share the dashboard layout. They use `c.get('cms').pluginCms('<name>')`. `ui.ts` can export `slots` with components for `dashboard.overview`, and `blocks` with a component per block type, which the site renders with `{ block }`.

A plugin runs only when its schema is migrated and an administrator grants what the manifest requests (`/dashboard/plugins`); an upgrade that requests more needs a new grant, and disabling removes the grants. Builds of CMS applications run the plugin policy lints (`cossack plugins check`): raw FastQL, the FastDB client, undeclared network hosts, permissions, resources or hooks, and host secrets fail the build. `cossack <plugin>:<command>` runs a command in the application as a signed-in dashboard user.

guides.title: Use CMS auth, sessions and ledgers
guides.summary: The scaffolded src/auth.ts runs @cossackframework/auth on CMS users and FastDB sessions; createCmsAuth() does the same for hand-written apps, and the host provides the session bag and ledgers.
guides.markdown:
With the `cms` feature, the scaffold renders the shared `auth` and `dashboard` pages over CMS storage: `src/auth.ts` exports the same functions as the database variant (`loginUser`, `registerUser`, `requestPasswordReset`, `resetPassword`, `listUserSessions`, …), backed by `cms.users` and `cms.authSessions`. Starting a session records the user's `lastSignInAt`, which outlives the session; `sessionsOf`, `revokeSessionOf` and `revokeSessionsOf` serve the user screen's Sessions tab, and `createApiToken`, `listApiTokens` and `revokeApiToken` its Application passwords tab; only the user and administrators see them (`canManageAccess`). An application password acts as its user, so give an integration its own user with a narrow role. Registration follows the General settings' "Anyone can register" and default role; reset tokens are stored as SHA-256 hashes and one request can use each.

`createCmsAuth(cms)` returns the auth middleware, a session manager on the `cms_auth_sessions` table (keyed by token, so rotation is one conditional update and exactly one concurrent rotation wins), `signIn`, `signOut`, a realtime descriptor provider whose public reference survives rotation while the fingerprint does not, and `principal(c)` for the request. Users and roles live in relational tables; `cms.users` creates, lists, searches, updates and deletes users, manages roles, verifies passwords with `@cossackframework/auth`'s hasher and resolves roles into a principal. `DEFAULT_ROLES` are Administrator, Editor, Author and Subscriber.

`cms.sessions` is the framework session bag with one row per key, so concurrent writes to different keys never overwrite each other. `cms.oauthStates` consumes OAuth state with one conditional delete. `cms.jobs()` and `cms.notifications()` are the core SQL ledgers on FastDB. `FileService` keeps bytes in Cossack object storage and ownership in FastDB, with a `sweep()` that finishes or cleans up interrupted uploads and deletes.

`cms:users` manages accounts and `cms:roles` defines roles and chooses users' roles; the dashboard lets a user manager without `cms:roles` add users only with the default role and keeps accounts that can manage roles out of its reach. `cms.uploadAvatar(userId, file, { principal })` stores a still or animated profile picture (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, AVIF; 5 MB) in the media library for the user themself or a user manager, sets it on the user and returns its URL.

guides.title: Schedule, preview, revise, redirect, translate and moderate CMS content
guides.summary: Scheduled entries and maintenance publishing, preview links, autosaves, revision restore and diffs, automatic and managed redirects, application passwords, signed webhooks, comments, patterns, languages and image variants on the CMS host.
guides.markdown:
**Scheduling.** Saving `published` with a future `publishedAt` stores `scheduled`; `cms.publishDue()` (run by maintenance every minute) publishes due entries as `system:scheduler`, so outbox events and webhooks fire then. `pending` means pending review. Visitors read `published` only.

**Previews and autosave.** `cms.createPreviewLink(resource, id, principal)` returns a 7-day token stored as its SHA-256; `cms.previewByToken(token)` reads the entry whatever its status, and `revokePreviewLinks` ends them. `cms.autosave(resource, id | 'new', principal, values)`, `latestAutosave` and `discardAutosave` keep one autosave per user and entry.

**Revisions.** `repository.revision(id, n)`, `repository.restore(id, n, { expectedRevision })` (keeps status, publication time, slug, nesting and language) and `compareRecords(fields, before, after)` / `diffWords(a, b)` for word-level diffs.

**Redirects.** When a published entry's URL changes, the update's batch records a 301 from the old URL, retargets redirects to it and drops one from the new URL; path changes of collections and taxonomies add prefix redirects (`/old/*` to `/new/*`). `cms.redirects.match(path)` serves paths without content; `save`, `list`, `delete` and `hit` manage them. Statuses: 301, 302, 307, 308 and 410.

**API and webhooks.** `cms.apiTokens.create(userId, { name, scope })` returns `cms_<id>.<secret>` once; `cms.tokenPrincipal(token)` resolves it (read-only tokens may only GET). `cms.webhooks.save({ name, url, events, collections })` subscribes to `entry.created`, `entry.updated`, `entry.published`, `entry.unpublished` and `entry.deleted`; deliveries are queued from the outbox and sent by `cms.webhooks.dispatch()` with `X-Cossack-Signature: sha256=` HMAC of `<timestamp>.<body>` (check with `verifyWebhookSignature`), retried over six attempts.

**Comments.** `cms.postComment(input, { principal, ip })` applies Settings → Discussion (sign-in, name and email, closing after N days, thread depth, moderation of all or first-time commenters, links, disallowed words) and a 15-second throttle per address; `cms.moderateComments(ids, status | 'delete', principal)` needs `cms:comments`.

**Patterns and languages.** The built-in `patterns` collection holds reusable rich text; a `core/pattern` block references a synced one. `cms.saveLanguages({ default, others }, principal)` sets the site's languages; other languages' URLs get a `/<code>` prefix from `entryUrls`, `cms.translations(collection, record)` maps languages to entries and `cms.translateEntry(collection, id, locale, principal)` starts a draft translation.

**Images.** Pass `images: ImageTransformer` (the Images binding on Workers, sharp on Node) to `createCMS`; `cms.files.variant(id, { width, height, accept })` makes and keeps resized AVIF/WebP variants, `setEdits(id, { crop, focus })` crops and sets the focal point, and `imageSrcset(file)` lists variants for `srcset`.

**Sign-in security.** `cms.security` keeps authenticator secrets (`startTotp`, `confirmTotp`, `verifyCode`), recovery codes, passkeys and short-lived challenges for pending sign-ins.
